Name: Ahreum Lee
Title: Gui, the Ghost
Bio:
Ahreum Lee is an interdisciplinary media artist, musician, game maker, and educator originally from Seoul and currently based in Tiohtià:ke/Mooniyang/Montréal. Her practice examines how everyday technologies mediate emotion, memory, social relations, and ecological systems. Working across games, 3D animation, web art, sound, installation, and performance, she often transforms familiar technological behaviours into rituals, speculative narratives, and participatory situations.

Her work has been presented at Arsenal Art Contemporain as part of the International Digital Art Biennial, Fonderie Darling, Ada X, the Leonard and Bina Ellen Art Gallery, Third Shift Festival, and Axis Lab. She has participated in programs and residencies at the Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity, Eastern Bloc, the Musée des beaux-arts de Montréal, and transmediale at ZK/U Berlin. In 2019, she was a finalist for the Emerging Digital Artist Award presented by EQ Bank and Trinity Square Video.
Description: Gui, the Ghost" is a text-adventure survival game inspired by the Korean folklore figure Cheo-Nyeo Gui Shin. Players inhabit Gui, a dead young woman trying to leave this world, becoming increasingly transparent as they recover her memories. How others react to Gui mirrors how societies fear, exclude, and construct “others.”

Name: Cade Anderson
Title: An Attribution
Bio:
Cade Anderson is a programmer of games with a fondness for limitation-bred-creativity and the not-yet-tried. He loves writing about strange worlds with weird rules. He believes that unsanded edges are a feature of interesting games. A few hands will get splinters- and that’s okay. He shares his creative process at www.cade.quest

Art is better together and he looks forward to building community and contributing to the grassroots, local art scenes.
Description:
You are in proximity of an interactive story about the journey to discern the nature of 1,300 grams of strange gelatin.

AN ATTRIBUTION is a tiny story that grows beyond the sum of its parts through non-linearity. The tale must be navigated and bushwhacked by the reader.

Name: Dustin Harvey
Title: ALONE TOGETHER
Bio:
Dustin Harvey is a Dartmouth-based artist working across film, theatre, and immersive performance. He is the founder of XOSECRET, where he creates participatory and site-responsive works presented across Canada and internationally. His work includes ALONE TOGETHER, a mobile app performance presented by SXSW, IDFA DocLab, MIT Docubase, and Belfast XR. His current mixed-reality project, AWAKE & STILL DROWNING, was presented at the Guanajuato International Film Festival, where it received the Best VR Experience award.

Across his work, Dustin is interested in what happens when an audience is given something to do: a simple instruction, a role to play, a place to go, or another person to pay attention to.
Description: ALONE TOGETHER is an episodic interactive performance for mobile phones where audiences play a professional stand-in, hired to enter the lives of people seeking companionship. Using voice recognition and AI, each encounter unfolds differently. For this exhibition, audiences experience the work from inside a small Alone Together Agency office cubicle.

Name: Em Jolly
Title: piss like a racehorse
Bio: Em Jolly is a multimedia maker currently working in Kjipuktuk, NS. They are completing their BFA in Expanded Media at NSCAD University. Following their studies in graphic design and digital arts, they turned towards the conceptual art avenue for post-secondary studies. They looked to find intersections of sensory technology and experience with media production. In April 2025, they lost all their previous physical work in a house fire, which shifted their attention to impermanent installations and documentation. Rooted in memory, access, loss and critique of value, their work attempts to intersect clashing media at the expense of artistic language. While their aesthetic is informed by materiality, lately they’ve enjoyed playfully queering contradictions of public bathrooms, through interactivity and collaboration.
Description:
Race against your neighbour's stream, defeat the reigning champ, and have your horse cross the finish line first. A carnival game of playful competition through pressure, release, dominance, gender fluidity and urinal etiquette.  

Have you won any pissing contests lately?

Name: Everest Pipkin
Title: The Poppy Grower
Bio: Everest Pipkin is a writer, game developer, artist, and educator whose work both in the studio and in the garden follows themes of ecology, tool making, and fantasies of collapse and isolation– as well as the labor, maintenance, devotion, and collective care so often present in those fantasies. They produce printed material as books and zines, as well as digital work for the browser and in game engines. They also make drawings on paper.
Description: The Poppy Grower is a browser-based game where you play an agricultural worker farming poppies alone on an asteroid. Told entirely through the interface of the proprietary operating system on asteroid, The Poppy Grower is a farm management sim and journaling game that is played in the actions of using your computer every day and documented in the shipping manifests.

Name: Mailey Horner
Title: Party in the Front, Disaster in the Back: a Fucking Didactic Textile Archive
Bio: Mailey Horner is an interdisciplinary artist working with sculpture, installation, drawing, bookarts, and textiles. She is interested in relating material practice with digital knowledge systems, data collection, labour, the body, and forms of enclosure. She holds a BA in English and Visual Studies from the University of Toronto, and is currently pursuing an MFA at NSCAD, studying the materiality of textiles as a cultural dataset that connects body, land, and material through moments of absence and dialectical negativity. She has exhibited nationally and internationally at the University of Lethbridge Art Gallery, The Manchester Metropolitan University, Casa Lethbridge, and The Anna Leonowens Gallery.

Name: Marcus Dénommé
Title: Desire Paths
Bio: Marcus Dénommé is a graphic artist from the Timiskaming region of North Eastern Ontario. Their practice is focused on the stamp and stencil as a tool of communication for the graphic/visual language within their artwork. Dénommé is the designer/editor of the small book press Veins & Arterys, which has independently published a dozen artist’s books over the years. As of late, Dénommé is inspired by the neighbourhood fauna such as rodents and racoons when it comes to storing computer hard drives and other important belongings by hiding them in both holes in the ground as well as leafy canopies high in trees.
Description: Desire Paths is part performance score, part drawing exercise, part collaborative game that facilitates movement and direction towards creative process. “Desire paths” organically form in our towns and cities from repeated traffic, yet they also tell an important and all-encompassing story from the voice of our communities.

Name: Meagan Byrne
Title: TRIPtych
Bio:
Meagan (pronounced: Me-Eh-Gan) is an Âpihtawikosisân (Fed: Métis of Ontario) game designer, interactive digital media artist, writer, and philosopher. Maturing as an artist on a steady diet of what they describe as “weird, chronically-online, Alt pop art” she uses the medium of video games, utilizing found digital 3D objects, set/lighting design and game mechanics to craft interactive environments. Their works explore one of two streams: expression of childhood trauma and Indigenous futurism (specifically Land Back utopianism).
Beyond digital interactive works Meagan is also known for her philosophical articles on Indigenous digital media such as “Read-Only Sacred Spaces: Indigenous Video Games as Space Safe from Vandalism and Theft” and more recently “What Makes it Indigenous? On Readability and Forced Readability in Indigenous Media”. Meagan is currently an MFA Studio Arts student at the University of Guelph.

Name: ray
Title: Time Travel has always been possible
Bio:
Ray (they/them) is an artist and cultural worker based in Montreal. Their work includes interactive media, coded websites, zines, and community-engaged projects. Ray focuses on building work that emphasizes intimacy, care, and accessibility, and explores how technology shapes emotional and social life.

They use DIY and poetic coding methods to create small interactive tools and participatory experiences. Ray’s background in facilitation, social practice and public programming informs their collaborative approach to working with communities and collectives. 🌀 learning → making → teaching as a spiral.
Description:
If archives desire immortality, what does the keyboard desire as their mediator? 'Time Travel Has Always Been Possible' is a poetic interactive hardware installation made with 30 years of feminist media arts footage from the Ada X archives. Turning the archive into a playable interface, the work explores how moving-image archives can be navigated through chance, tactility, and play. 

Pressing a key activates a specific piece of footage; pressing it again moves to another point in its timeline. The cyberfeminist keyboard is hand made (cardboard, packaging materials, nail extensions, and scavenged electronics) draws on punk DIY and feminist histories of making technology. Handwired and hand-coded, the keyboard becomes both interface and sculptural object. And for myself, how can social practice facilitation use technology to mediate conversations, vs the labour of 'presence'?

Name: Shihab Mian
Title: could you understand me leaving?
Bio: Shihab Mian (she-hub me-in, he/him) is a game developer & creative technologist working primarily with creative programming & game engines. He is intrigued by the emotionality of technology and how it shapes human connection. He creates deprecated programs and intentional failings, where inefficiency, glitch, or error are embraced.
Description: A home exists as a reflection of those who've lived in it. How does a home dictate the way we act, how does it affect the perception of our memories? An empty house screams with a blaring alarm, begging for attention over and over. Who implemented this alarm? Who was it intended for? What are they trying to tell us? Can we turn it off? How can I ignore it?
